test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A train 'R' leaves Chennai at 5 a.m. and reaches Vijayawada at 12 p.m. Another train 'S' leaves Vijayawada at 7 a.m. and reaches Chennai at 5:30 p.m. At what time do the two trains cross each other?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by **Train R** = 7 hours; Time taken by **Train S** = 10.5 hours.

Let the total distance be **LCM**(7, 10.5) = 21 units.

Speed of R = 21 ÷ 7 = 3 units/hr; Speed of S = 21 ÷ 10.5 = 2 units/hr.

Distance covered by R by 7 a.m. (in 2 hours) = 3 × 2 = 6 units.

Remaining distance = 21 − 6 = 15 units. Time to meet = 15 ÷ (3 + 2) = 3 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Departure of **Train R** (Chennai) = 5 a.m.; Arrival at **Vijayawada** = 12 p.m.

Departure of **Train S** (Vijayawada) = 7 a.m.; Arrival at **Chennai** = 5:30 p.m.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time | Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Speed₁ + Speed₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de833846b482a7654c92194a9e683434734a0c6478f14ef9d5fa5b70068953d8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Travel time for **Train R** = 12 p.m. − 5 a.m. = 7 hours

⇒ Travel time for **Train S** = 5:30 p.m. − 7 a.m. = 10.5 hours = 21/2 hours

⇒ Let Distance = D; SpeedR = D/7 and SpeedS = D/(21/2) = 2D/21

⇒ Distance covered by R in 2 hours (5 a.m. to 7 a.m.) = (D/7) × 2 = 2D/7

⇒ Remaining Distance at 7 a.m. = D − 2D/7 = 5D/7

⇒ Relative Speed = D/7 + 2D/21 = (3D + 2D)/21 = 5D/21

⇒ Time taken to meet after 7 a.m. = (5D/7) ÷ (5D/21) = (5D/7) × (21/5D) = 3 hours

⇒ **Meeting Time** = 7 a.m. + 3 hours = 10 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Principle

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Meeting Time Calculation

To find the meeting time, always equalize the **starting time** of both objects by calculating the distance covered by the first object before the second starts.

LCM Method for Distance

Assuming distance as the **LCM** of individual travel times simplifies calculations by avoiding complex algebraic variables and fractions.</p
